responses.content: Looking for the leap year check.
is_leap_year() excludes every century year; it misses the 400-year rule. Adding it.

tool_calls.name: edit_file
tool_calls.arguments: {"path": "dates.py", "old": "    return year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0\n", "new": "    return year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0)\n"}

responses.content: is_leap_year() now treats century years divisible by 400 as leap years, so days_in_month(2000, 2) is 29. 1900 stays a common year.
